Never reset or destructively rewrite the database; use additive migrations, explicit backfills, versioned records, feature flags, audit events and compensating actions.

Tourify platform consent must never imply cooperative membership, data contribution, ownership transfer, voting delegation, fiduciary relationship, research participation, representation authority or collective-licensing authority.

The cooperative or data-governance entity must be legally and operationally separable from Tourify, with its own governing documents, membership ledger, finances, board approvals, conflicts process and termination procedures.

Every data use requires an active purpose-specific contribution licence or permission, valid consent where applicable, source lineage, retention rule, output policy and revocation/withdrawal treatment.

No raw or member-identifiable cooperative data may be exposed to external researchers or other members unless the governing documents, law, consent, contract and access policy explicitly authorize it.
No current or future member-specific price, rate, bid, negotiation position or competitively sensitive term may enter shared benchmarks, research outputs or group recommendations.
Research access is default-deny and must pass ethics, privacy, security, competition, intellectual-property, export, purpose and output-review gates.
External registries, research institutions, regulators, standards organizations, courts, CMOs and administrators remain authoritative for their own records.

Cooperative benefit allocation, patronage treatment, grants, stipends, rebates or distributions must be approved by counsel, tax advisers, the governing board and the applicable member process before activation.

Membership interests, voting rights, patronage allocations, tokens or credits may not be marketed as investments or transferable financial instruments without a separate securities analysis and approval package.
Collective licensing, bargaining, representation, lobbying and public-policy advocacy each require separately approved authority, entity, mandate, jurisdiction and communications controls.
No automated legal, contract, tax, policy, investment or research-ethics advice may be delivered as a professional conclusion.
Every external submission, research licence, dataset release, publication, standards proposal, vote, distribution and authority change must be idempotent, versioned, attributable and auditable.

Stop publication or external action when consent is invalid, a cohort is too small, one participant dominates, source data is stale, re-identification risk is unacceptable, competition review is incomplete, authority is missing or the output could be understood as coordinated pricing or legal instruction.
